messages:
maria: Quick ping — PR #412 landed the Dedicated provisioning rewrite. Can someone do a11y pass and sanity-check the autoscale example? I'm worried the YAML could mislead folks about min/max burst.

devin: I can look today. Which file? link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412

maria: It's the section under docs/dedicated/provisioning.md — section "Autoscaling policy examples". Also the SLA blurb needs simpler language for customer-facing pages.

kevin: I'm skimmed the YAML, the burst example might imply unlimited scaling if you read it fast. Suggest we add an explicit "burst capacity is bounded by reserved pools" sentence.

samir: I have a quick wording suggestion for SLA: "We aim for 99.9% availability for Dedicated endpoints; scheduled maintenance may be excluded and will be announced 72 hours in advance." Too legalese?

maria: That's clearer. Maybe replace "may be excluded" with "does not apply during scheduled maintenance" — more direct.

devin: Autoscale snippet tweak (proposal):
```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 20
  burst_limit: 8   # bounded by reserved_pool_size
  metrics:
    - type: rps
      target: 120
```
Add the comment for burst limit and a link to reserved pool docs.

kevin: +1. Also add a short note about isolation: "Dedicated capacity provides tenant isolation; evicted workloads are reported to the tenant admin and automatically retried per retry policy." Keeps expectations clear.

maria: Can someone add an a11y checklist line — e.g., "use plain language, avoid passive voice, provide examples for acronyms (SLA, RPS)". I'll do a pass after PR update.

docs-bot: build status — docs build succeeded for PR #412 (:white_check_mark:)

samir: I'll open a small follow-up PR with the YAML tweak + SLA wording and a11y checklist item.

maria: Awesome, thanks — ping here when it's up and I'll do final sign-off :thumbsup:
